transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Santos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Alyssa Chen (TideWell CTO), Ramon Ortega (Platform Eng), Sofia Patel (Security), Ben Walker (Product)
---
Summary:
Short sync to hand off the connector packaging and marketplace onramp tasks. Goal: agree on Helm packaging, KMS compatibility, VPC peering pattern, telemetry/usage metering expectations, and UAT schedule.
Topics discussed:
- Helm chart and values.yaml layout
- Marketplace listing constraints & billing SKU mapping
- Private deployment (VPC) networking and egress
- KMS/HSM compatibility and rotation flow
- Telemetry and token-level cost data for usage dashboards
- Pilot UAT and performance guardrails (latency/cost tradeoffs)
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Morgan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to do a quick - handshake and get the ops handoff moving along. Diego and Priya from our side are the tech leads on packaging and listing.
[00:12] Alyssa Chen: great, thanks Morgan. We've been eager to get the marketplace listing done, plus we need the connector to run in our VPC with our KMS.
[00:20] Diego Santos: yeah, hi all. quick agenda: helm chart PR, marketplace metadata files, kms compatibility notes, and then telemetry/usage outputs. we'll flag any blockers.
[00:31] Ramon Ortega: one thing up front — our infra team uses strict egress rules, so any listing that calls home has to go via approved egress nat. also we prefer S3 presigned uploads for model artifacts, not open pulls.
[00:45] Priya Nair: noted. our helm chart supports imagePullSecrets and can be configured to use internal registries; we'll include example values for presigned flows and for private registries.
[00:54] Sofia Patel: on KMS — we use an HSM-backed KMS and we need to ensure key rotation won't break cached model keys. do you support envelope encryption or do you expect customer keys in env vars?
[01:10] Diego Santos: good q. Redwood's private package supports envelope keys via KMS APIs; the current connector has a key manager interface, but we need to validate HSM vendor specifics. we'll send a compatibility checklist.
[01:22] Ben Walker: also curious about cost telemetry — we'd like token-level breakdowns fed to our billing pipeline for showback. what do you export for consumption?
[01:34] Morgan Lee: we export per-request token counts, latency, model id, and route tags. for private deployments we can ship a lightweight forwarder to push to your metrics endpoint or S3.
[01:46] Alyssa Chen: can it be configurable to redact PII? our security team insists on no raw prompt data leaving the VPC.
[01:56] Diego Santos: yes, the forwarder includes scrub rules; by default we only emit token counts and model metadata, not prompt text. we'll add the scrub config to the values.yaml.
[02:08] Ramon Ortega: networking pattern — what's your recommended VPC peering vs. PrivateLink? we run in AWS and prefer routes that don't rely on internet egress.
[02:18] Priya Nair: for marketplace listing we typically support both: PrivateLink endpoints for managed hosted routes, or direct peering for private deployments. since you're doing private deploy, peering plus NATed egress for external artifacts is fine. we'll document both patterns.
[02:32] Sofia Patel: audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for model access and config changes. Can Redwood forward those to our CloudWatch or Splunk?
[02:42] Diego Santos: yes, we can forward audit events to CloudWatch logs or a syslog endpoint. they'll include user, action, timestamp, and request id. we'll confirm retention policy options in the checklist.
[02:56] Ben Walker: on the marketplace metadata: we need the SKU mapping and how usage-based billing will surface in our ledgers. do you have example files?
[03:07] Morgan Lee: Priya will share the marketplace packaging checklist which includes SKU template and delta mapping for reserved vs usage tiers. we'll include a sample invoice payload.
[03:18] Alyssa Chen: operationally, for the UAT, we want to do a week-long run with 3 different load patterns: low-latency interactive, high-throughput batch, and mixed. how do you recommend configuring KV cache and batching?
[03:33] Diego Santos: for interactive low-latency, set max-batch-size=1 and prefer prefix caching; for throughput batch, bump batch size and enable async dispatch; we can provide suggested profiles in the helm chart under 'profiles'.
[03:47] Ramon Ortega: any special kernel/quantization constraints? we plan to use quantized models for cost reasons but want to know the perf delta.
[03:56] Priya Nair: we have model variant guidance in the refarch doc; quantization reduces memory and cost but can add mild latency on some hardware. we'll attach benchmarking spreadsheet with expected token/s throughput per GPU class.
[04:12] Sofia Patel: regarding secrets, rotation: we rotate KMS every 30 days. If the KV cache is encrypted with customer key, will rotation trigger a cache flush?
[04:25] Diego Santos: rotation doesn't invalidate the whole cache; we rewrap keys during rotation where possible. but we'll note limits: some rotations may require restart depending on HSM integration. add that to the checklist.
[04:40] Ben Walker: what about the helm lifecycle — how do we handle upgrades during canary? we have a zero-downtime requirement.
[04:50] Priya Nair: our chart supports rolling upgrades with pre/post hooks. for stateful cache you can use a sidecar that preserves KV across upgrades; we also support canary labels to route a % of traffic to new pods. we'll include example kustomize overlays.
[05:03] Alyssa Chen: ok, would love to see the example values and a simple deploy script we can run in our staging.
[05:11] Morgan Lee: Diego will open a helm PR with README and a deploy script. link will be in follow-up.
[05:18] Ramon Ortega: security scan — we run Clair and Trivy in our pipeline. do you publish SBOMs for images?
[05:26] Diego Santos: yes, we publish SBOMs and signed manifests for official images; when we hand over a connector image we can provide the SBOM and digest.
[05:35] Sofia Patel: for marketplace listing, any compliance paperwork needed? SOC2 attestation or ISO?
[05:42] Morgan Lee: Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO-27001 summary, and our penetration test results. we'll send the package to TideWell security.
[05:53] Ben Walker: on tagging/labels for cost allocation — do you support per-customer tenant labels so we can parse in billing?
[05:58] Priya Nair: yes, we emit route and tenant labels; the forwarder can enrich metrics with your account ids.
[06:07] Alyssa Chen: thinking of performance, how do you handle fallback variants? suppose the high-quality variant isn't available in a region; can Redwood route to cheaper quantized variant automatically?
[06:19] Diego Santos: yes, policy-based routing supports fallback chains based on latency/cost constraints. that's configured in the route policy manifest; we'll share an example that suits your SLA.
[06:30] Ramon Ortega: that's helpful. another nit: our legal team wants to ensure model artifacts never land on public buckets; presigned S3 is OK but only to internal S3.
[06:40] Morgan Lee: we can adapt the artifact flow to use your internal S3 endpoints only; will call that out in the values.yaml and docs.
[06:48] Ben Walker: for the UAT acceptance criteria — can we define latency percentiles and token cost thresholds?
[06:55] Priya Nair: yes, we'll propose SLA checklists: p50, p90, p99 latencies for each profile, and per-token cost not exceeding the mapped SKU threshold.
[07:06] Alyssa Chen: great. any known issues with on-prem customers and RBAC? we use an internal LDAP + SAML federation.
[07:15] Diego Santos: Redwood supports SAML SSO and LDAP sync; for private deployments we recommend SAML with SCIM for user provisioning. we'll include a SAML example.
[07:25] Ramon Ortega: do you support per-request debugging traces? we need tracing for root cause during UAT.
[07:31] Priya Nair: yes, tracing hooks are available; we can send traces to your X-Ray or Jaeger endpoints. by default traces are sampled; you can enable full trace capture in staging.
[07:45] Ben Walker: one more thing — billing reconciliation: how do we reconcile usage vs reserved? if we overrun the reserved capacity in a pilot window, what's the overage handling?
[07:55] Morgan Lee: the marketplace listing includes both reserved SKU and overage SKU mapping. overages are billed at the usage SKU rate; for pilots we'll work with you on a temporary grace allocation so you can run tests without surprise invoices.
[08:08] Alyssa Chen: ok this all sounds good. can we confirm timeline? we'd like to start UAT the week of 2026-05-25.
[08:15] Morgan Lee: yes, timeline is workable. immediate next steps are: Diego's helm PR (target 05/17), Priya's marketplace packaging docs (05/18), TideWell sends VPC/egress diagram (05/19), then a follow-up UAT kickoff for 05/20 or 05/21.
[08:34] Ramon Ortega: sounds good. I'll coordinate the infra availability.
[08:38] Sofia Patel: security will review the KMS checklist when it's shared. please include rotation caveats.
[08:45] Diego Santos: will do — I'll mark the items in the PR and the checklist.
[08:50] Ben Walker: for the helm PR, can you include a minimal values file for each of the three profiles? low-latency, batch, mixed.
[08:58] Priya Nair: yes. we'll add profile values under charts/tidewell/values-*.yaml.
[09:05] Morgan Lee: ok let's go to a couple of quick technical deep-dive points — Diego?
[09:09] Diego Santos: sure. first, the KV cache persistence: we use an LRU backed by WAL for fast restart; in private deploys we optionally persist the KV to a PVC or an external Redis. volume mount examples will be in the chart.
[09:23] Ramon Ortega: PVCs are preferred; our ops can expose an EBS-backed PVC. what about resizing during a scale event?
[09:30] Diego Santos: we rely on Kubernetes dynamic provisioning; resizing requires CSI support. for short bursts we use burst capacity with stateless workers and shared cache on Redis.
[09:40] Alyssa Chen: will Redis introduce cross-instance latency?
[09:43] Priya Nair: minimal if colocated; for multi-AZ you may want a managed Redis cluster with replication. we'll recommend topology.
[09:51] Ben Walker: about autoscaling — can the chart plumb HPA based on token-per-second metrics?
[09:58] Diego Santos: yes, we emit a custom metric tidewell.tokens_per_second per pod; HPA can scale on that. example HPA manifest in repo.
[10:06] Sofia Patel: data residency — we need confirmation that logs forwarded don't include user prompt; you said scrub rules exist but can you ensure redaction before leaving VPC?
[10:15] Diego Santos: scrub happens at the forwarder prior to egress; we provide regex-based scrubbing and PII tokenization. we'll include default scrubs and note how to extend them.
[10:26] Morgan Lee: ok, wrapping up the tech points — last one is Canary routing: you can set a canary percentage or an explicit header to route. Diego, will we include an example operator manifest?
[10:36] Diego Santos: yes. example: route policy manifest with fallback chain and canary percentage. PR will have that.
[10:43] Ben Walker: thanks. any other open questions from TideWell?
[10:47] Alyssa Chen: just to reiterate, get the PR + the KMS checklist and we'll do an internal security review.
[10:52] Sofia Patel: and include pen-test results and SOC2.
[10:55] Morgan Lee: will do. ok, let's go to recap and next steps.
[11:00] Recap:
- Diego to open helm chart PR with profiles, example values, SBOM and CHART README by 2026-05-17.
- Priya to send marketplace packaging & SKU mapping doc by 2026-05-18.
- Morgan to share SOC2/ISO and pen-test package to Sofia by 2026-05-18.
- TideWell (Alyssa/Ramon) to provide VPC diagram and egress policy by 2026-05-19.
- Schedule UAT kickoff on or around 2026-05-20 (TBD).
[11:28] Final confirmations and polite sign-off.
[11:35] Morgan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the PR and docs.
[11:40] Alyssa Chen: thanks, talk soon.
